model: Airthings sensors via Weble WBox G110 BACnet IP gateway
applies_to: Airthings for Business sensors whose data is pulled from the Airthings MQTT service by a Weble WBox G110 and served on BACnet IP.
summary: A Weble WBox G110 subscribes to the Airthings for Business MQTT service and creates BACnet IP Analog Input objects for every Airthings device in the account. Each device gets a block of 20 AIs: CO2, humidity, light, PM1, PM10, PM2.5, pressure, differential pressure, radon, sound, temperature, VOC and lux, with 14-20 reserved. Objects are only created for sensors the device actually has.
notes: Listed for the first Airthings device (AI 1-13). Each further device uses the next block of 20: device 2 = AI 21-33, device 3 = AI 41-53 (instance = 20 x (device - 1) + n).
Object names start with the Airthings device serial number, e.g. 2930012345_co2.
AI 14-20 are reserved for future sensors and are not created.
The guide's descriptions for AI 05 (pm10) and AI 06 (pm25) are swapped; the descriptions here follow the object names.
Radon units are printed as Becquerels.
Source is the Airthings developer web page (not a PDF), updated 2026-11.

integration.summary: Create an MQTT client in the Airthings for Business dashboard, load the Airthings template on the WBox G110 and let it build the objects from incoming data. Read the AIs for each device block; back up the gateway once all objects exist so instances survive a replacement.
setup: BACnet server runs on eth0 by default (192.168.1.99); eth1 uses DHCP. Change the interface in the Airthings BACnet Server settings.
Needs WBox G110 licences for MQTT, BACnet and Remote Services, plus Internet access (Ethernet or USB 3G/4G modem).
Objects can be exported as EDE, CSV or JSON from the gateway once created.
gotchas: Objects are created on first data, so a sensor a device lacks never appears.
Removed devices keep their objects but stop updating; re-adding the device resumes the same instances.
Save a gateway backup after objects are created, or a replacement gateway may number them differently.
